lessons.title: The colon: Shift + semicolon
lessons.tip: The colon is on the same key as the semicolon: hold Shift with your left little finger and press the key with your right little finger.

tuto.intro: The colon introduces a list or an explanation. On QWERTY, it shares the semicolon key: you get it with Shift. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Hold Shift with your left little finger (the opposite hand), press the semicolon key with your right little finger, then release.
In English, you never put a space before : ; ? or !. It goes word, sign, space. The sign sticks to the word before it.
Here is my list: bread, milk, rice. The colon announces what follows: a list, an explanation, a quotation.

tuto.tip: Goal: type the colon with Shift + semicolon, tucked tight against the word before it.

lessons.text: Here is my list: bread, milk, rice. Three words: calm, kind, quiet. Note: it is late. Look: the sun is out. Remember: stay calm. Two things: tea, milk.

lessons.title: The apostrophe
lessons.tip: The apostrophe is the key to the right of the semicolon, typed with your right little finger. On a US International keyboard, it is a dead key: press it, then the space bar.

tuto.intro: The apostrophe marks a contraction (don't, it's, she's) or possession. It is very common in English. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.t: To the right of the semicolon
rules.d: It is typed with your right little finger, on the key just right of the semicolon, without Shift.
On US International, the apostrophe is a dead key: press it, then the space bar, otherwise it combines with the next letter to make an accented letter. On a plain US keyboard, it works straight away.
Type the start, the apostrophe, the end, with no space at all: don't, it's, can't, she's, they're.

tuto.tip: Goal: type the apostrophe with the right movement for your keyboard, with no space around it.

lessons.text: It's late and she's tired. We don't know. She can't come, but she's glad. That's fine. They're here.

lessons.title: The hyphen
lessons.tip: The hyphen is the key to the right of the 0, at the top right: your right little finger reaches up to it, without Shift. It joins compound words.

tuto.intro: The hyphen joins compound words (part-time, well-known, check-in, mother-in-law). The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Your right little finger reaches up to the key to the right of the 0, without Shift. That is the hyphen key.
No space around the hyphen: mother-in-law, part-time, well-known, check-in.

rules.t: Do not confuse it with the underscore
rules.d: The underscore (_) on the same key needs Shift: it comes later, with the symbols. Here, it is the plain hyphen.

tuto.tip: Goal: reach up to the hyphen with your right little finger and return to the home row.

lessons.text: Her mother-in-law has a part-time job in a well-known shop near the check-in desk. We eat ice cream. She has a T-shirt.

lessons.title: The question mark: Shift + forward slash
lessons.tip: The question mark is on the same key as the forward slash: hold Shift with your left little finger and press the key with your right little finger.

tuto.intro: The question mark ends a question. On QWERTY, it shares the forward slash key: you get it with Shift. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Hold Shift with your left little finger, press the forward slash key with your right little finger, then release.
In English, you never put a space before : ; ? or !. It goes word, sign, space. The sign sticks to the word before it.
Where is the dog? What is your name? A single question mark at the end of the question is enough.

tuto.tip: Goal: type ? with Shift + forward slash, tucked tight against the last word.

lessons.text: Where is the dog? What is your name? How old are you? Do you like tea? Is it cold? Can you help? Who is there?

lessons.title: The exclamation mark: Shift + 1
lessons.tip: The exclamation mark is on the 1 key, at the top left: hold Shift with your right little finger and press 1 with your left little finger.

tuto.intro: The exclamation mark sets the tone: emotion, an order, surprise. On QWERTY, it is on the 1 key: you get it with Shift. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Hold Shift with your right little finger (the opposite hand), press the 1 key with your left little finger, then release.
In English, you never put a space before : ; ? or !. It goes word, sign, space. The sign sticks to the word before it.
Stop! Well done! One exclamation mark is enough: avoid piling them up.

tuto.tip: Goal: type ! with Shift + 1, tucked tight against the last word.

lessons.text: Stop! Look out! Well done! What a day! Happy birthday! Welcome home! Good luck! Thank you! Hello!

lessons.title: Brackets and quotation marks
lessons.tip: Round brackets are on the 9 and 0 keys, and straight quotation marks are on the apostrophe key: all need Shift, held with your left little finger.

tuto.intro: Round brackets set aside an extra detail, and quotation marks surround speech. On QWERTY, all three need Shift, with keys on the right hand. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Hold Shift with your left little finger. The opening bracket is on 9, the closing bracket on 0, and the quotation mark on the apostrophe key.
Every bracket or quotation mark you open must be closed. Practise chaining the opening, the text, then the closing without hesitating.
They surround speech: He says: "hello". English uses these straight quotation marks on the keyboard.

tuto.tip: Goal: type ( ) and " with Shift, opening then closing.

lessons.text: Tom (ten) says: "hello". Anna (nine) says: "thanks" (again). Dad (at work) says: "wait" (please) (now).

lessons.title: Punctuation in real text
lessons.tip: You bring all the punctuation together in a real text. Spot the next mark in advance, and get ready with Shift if needed.

tuto.intro: You bring all the punctuation together in a lively text: hyphens, apostrophes, quotation marks, brackets, exclamation and question marks.

rules.t: Spot the mark that is coming
rules.d: Before you reach a mark, know which one it is: direct (apostrophe, hyphen, comma, full stop) or with Shift (? ! : ( ) ").
Each mark that needs Shift uses the Shift key opposite the mark's own key: it is the same rule as for capital letters.
Correct punctuation makes a text easy to read and professional. Take your time: speed will come.

tuto.tip: Goal: chain all the punctuation together in a text, without breaking your rhythm.

lessons.text: "Come quickly!" he says. She replies: "Wait for me; it's late." It is a well-known story (really). Who is there? Mum!
